archetypes.name: risk-integration
archetypes.rationale: The no-rounds behavior change from empty output to a section header is a silent contract break for any downstream consumer that tested for emptiness; this archetype checks caller update completeness and side effects.
archetypes.prompt_body: This diff changes the no-completed-rounds output from empty to `## Review Phase Detail\n\nNo review rounds completed.`. Examine whether every downstream consumer that formerly relied on empty output (archival log parsers, harness assertions, any shell callers checking `[ -s file ]` or `[ -z output ]`) was updated. Check whether `render-final-summary.sh`'s `mkdir -p plan-review` fallback side-effect could corrupt or interfere with the design tmpdir when the directory is later expected to be absent, or when concurrent runs share the same tmpdir. Verify that `write-final-report.sh` omits `--no-gantt` for final reports and that `progress_report.py` consistently passes it for live terminal output. Assess regression risk for the `assert_not_contains '## Review Phase Detail'` assertion that was flipped in `test-write-final-report.sh`. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: mermaid-format
archetypes.rationale: The gantt block generation involves domain-specific Mermaid protocol requirements (dateFormat X, integer start/end, axisFormat) that static correctness reviewers may not have the domain context to validate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the generated Mermaid gantt syntax for protocol correctness: verify that `dateFormat X` with zero-based integer relative-second start/end fields produces valid task lines and that Mermaid will not misinterpret them as duration-mode syntax. Check whether `axisFormat %%H:%%M:%%S` (with the `%%` printf escapes) resolves to a valid `axisFormat %H:%M:%S` directive in the final output. Review the `clean_label` AWK function in `render-review-phase-detail.sh` to confirm it strips all Mermaid-sensitive punctuation that could break task-line parsing (colons and commas are handled, but verify that characters like `[`, `]`, `#`, and semicolons are also neutralized). Verify that per-round task IDs (`r1_t1`, `r2_t1`, etc.) are unique within each gantt block and that having identically labeled tasks across rounds does not create ID collisions. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
